issues.legal_issue: A licensee does not acquire title by adverse possession merely by remaining in unauthorised possession after termination of the licence; the licensee must openly assert a hostile title.
material_facts: The occupant’s licence was terminated, after which he remained in possession of the premises.
The occupant claimed title by adverse possession, but there was no evidence that he asserted a hostile title after termination of the licence.
The occupant’s unauthorised possession had continued for more than twelve years.
The owner sought recovery of possession.
issues.conclusion: The occupant had not established title by adverse possession, and the suit for possession was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 65 of the Limitation Act, 1963, mere unauthorised possession following termination of a licence, even for more than twelve years, does not establish adverse possession. The licensee must perform an overt act showing an assertion of title hostile to the licensor. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.possession_recovery_suit_after_license_t: An owner brought a suit to recover possession after terminating the occupant’s licence.
predicates.licensee_claims_adverse_title: The former licensee claimed to have acquired title by adverse possession.
predicates.post_termination_hostile_assertion: After termination of the licence, the former licensee performed an overt act asserting title hostile to the owner.

issues.definition: When an owner sues for possession after terminating a licence and the former licensee claims adverse title without asserting it through an overt hostile act, adverse title is not established and the possession suit is not time-barred.
